SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: USES OF HEAT IN
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Uses of heat in helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: USES OF HEAT IN
Uses of heat in is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Identify uses of heat energy in the ironing, drying) environment  Learners to use multimedia

What this means
In this part you learn to identify uses of heat energy in the ironing, drying) environment  Learners to use multimedia. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify uses of heat energy in the ironing, drying) environment  Learners to use multimedia.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Uses of heat in” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify uses of heat energy in the ironing, drying) environment  Learners to use multimedia. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use heat energy responsibly to resources to find out uses on heat promote conservation and safety energy in daily life

What this means
In this part you learn to use heat energy responsibly to resources to find out uses on heat promote conservation and safety energy in daily life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use heat energy responsibly to resources to find out uses on heat promote conservation and safety energy in daily life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Uses of heat in matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use heat energy responsibly to resources to find out uses on heat promote conservation and safety energy in daily life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate conservation of heat  In groups,

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate conservation of heat  In groups,. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate conservation of heat  In groups,.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Uses of heat in this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate conservation of heat  In groups,. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Uses of heat in is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Uses of heat in” around your school. (skill: identify uses of heat energy in the ironing, drying) environment  Learners to use multimedia)

Example 2: Say why Uses of heat in matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: use heat energy responsibly to resources to find out uses on heat promote conservation and safety energy in daily life)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Uses of heat in this week. (skill: appreciate conservation of heat  In groups,)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Uses of heat in to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify uses of heat energy in the ironing, drying) environment  Learners to use multimedia.
3. Practise this skill: use heat energy responsibly to resources to find out uses on heat promote conservation and safety energy in daily life.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate conservation of heat  In groups,.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Uses of heat in from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Uses of heat in: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Uses of heat in?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is heat energy environment learner should be able to: energy (warming, cooking, used in daily life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Uses of heat in means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify uses of heat energy in the ironing, drying) environment  Learners to use multimedia.
5. Be able to: use heat energy responsibly to resources to find out uses on heat promote conservation and safety energy in daily life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
